questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What sourcing in a report is doing

stimulus.body: Contexte du texte : «Add separate primary sources for each claim.» A report makes three statistical claims but cites only a single vague blog post for all of them. L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Avec «Create a sourcing improvement / Primary sources per claim. / What sourcing in a report is doing» en téte, quelle option est conforme au texte ?

options.text: Add separate primary sources for each claim

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: each claim needs its own verifiable source; design, length, or style changes do not fix sourcing. On that basis "Add separate primary sources for each claim" is the supported choice. Option A ("Add more adjectives") fails because it confuses style with sourcing; Option B ("Increase the font size") fails because it confuses design with sourcing; Option D ("Shorten the report") fails because it confuses length with sourcing.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: What a fact-check verifies

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: «Primary evidence and reliable sources.» Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: Avec l’indice «Remember fact-check scope / Evidence. / What a fact-check verifies», quelle option est réellement appuyée par le texte ?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: fact-checks compare claims to primary evidence and reliable sources; appearance, design, or timing are irrelevant. On that basis "Primary evidence and reliable sources" is the supported choice. Option A ("The headline's font") fails because it confuses design with evidence; Option B ("The claimant's wardrobe") fails because it confuses appearance with evidence; Option C ("The posting schedule") fails because it confuses timing with evidence.

questions.topic: What a character limit does to a post
questions.learningObjective: Analyze a limit's effect on nuance

stimulus.body: Contexte du texte : «The conditions disappear from view.» A policy update with many conditions is posted under a tight character limit, leaving only the headline conclusion. L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Le passage est confronté à «Analyze a limit's effect on nuance / What gets lost? / What a character limit does to a post». Quelle réponse résiste ?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: a tight limit drops conditions, leaving only the conclusion; compression does not change law or font. On that basis "The conditions disappear from view" is the supported choice. Option A ("The font shrinks automatically") fails because it confuses text with typography; Option C ("The conclusion becomes longer") fails because it confuses compression with expansion; Option D ("The policy becomes law") fails because it confuses posting with legislation.

questions.topic: The disclosure an influencer owes

stimulus.body: L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. «Paid partnership with Brand X.» Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Le passage est confronté à «Create an adequate disclosure / Explicit and clear. / The disclosure an influencer owes». Quelle réponse résiste ?

options.misconception: selects "Check it out" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition
reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: explicit partnership language is adequate; vague thanks, bare tags, or calls to action are not. On that basis "Paid partnership with Brand X" is the supported choice. Option A ("Check it out") fails because it selects "Check it out" where the disclosure an influencer owes requires a different condition; Option B ("Thanks Brand X") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles the disclosure an influencer owes; Option D ("#sponsored") fails because it bare tag too vague.
